text:
Emma: follow-up to the RFC about distributed admission. want a concrete, low-latency path that keeps global fairness without blocking on central policy.
Emma: proposal sketch: tiny local sidecar does optimistic admits (fast), central policy engine reconciles async and issues corrections.
Raj: quick Q — if sidecar allows then central denies, how do we avoid double-charge and user-visible surprises?
Sarah: tradeoffs: central = stronger global fairness, local = <5ms fast-path. pick eventual consistency and compensating corrections rather than synchronous validation.
Mike: agree. interface boundary: sidecar.admit(req) => {decision: allow|deny|probe, token_id?, provisional?: true|false, backoff_ms?, policy_version, decision_id}. keep payload tiny.
Olivia: add decision_id to traces and logs so we can reconcile later. emit metric admit.provisional_count.
admission-bot: deploy: admission-sidecar v0.3 canary -> 5% traffic us-west-2 :rocket:
Emma: rollout plan: canary + dual-write reconciliation for 2w. threshold: mismatch_rate < 0.1% to promote. console toggle per-tenant to force central-only.
Raj: fairness composition: tenant_weight * route_weight * model_weight seems ok; need semantics when weights change.
Sarah: avoid global optimization—use reservoir buckets + decaying credits + soft-shed. approximate proportional fairness is acceptable.
Mike: example admit proto (tiny):
```
{
  "decision": "allow",
  "token_id": "tok-8f3e",
  "provisional": true,
  "backoff_ms": 0,
  "policy_version": "2026-03-18-1",
  "decision_id": "dec-20260318-abc123"
}
```
Olivia: fallback behaviour: if central later denies a provisional allow, sidecar should emit a compensating event (refund/charge correction) and apply soft-rate-limit to the session; avoid hard-kicking in most cases.
Emma: abuse signals: central detector streams short-lived modifiers (abuse_score) to sidecars; multiplier applied to backoff and fairness weight for N seconds.
Raj: telemetry — add admit.decision_latency_p95, admit.mismatch_rate, admit.provisional_ratio, abuse.score_internal and per-tenant reject_rate.
Sarah: failure modes: policy_version drift across sidecars. mitigations: periodic full sync, and a fast reconcile endpoint returning delta actions for last 5m.
Mike: migration steps: 1) sidecar v0.3 optimistic admits + logging; 2) dual-write central decisions and offline reconciliation; 3) enable auto-correct; 4) flip default to sidecar primary. owners: Emma (rollout), Raj (policy engine), Olivia (telemetry), Sarah (abuse), Mike (sidecar).
Olivia: dedicated-tenants note: reserved capacity should include quota_source=dedicated and bypass some fairness knobs but remain auditable.
Emma: for dedicated, use a signed_claim short-lived token that sidecar validates locally to avoid central roundtrips.
Raj: open Q: surface per-route fairness to product owners — need a console explain page + per-request explain logs (eg: why delayed).
Sarah: also offer SAFE mode opt-out: strict central-only admits for high-sensitivity workloads (no provisional).
Mike: i'll draft RFC follow-up with interface sketches, proto samples, metrics, and migration timeline. will add unit/integration tests.
Emma: target RFC draft EOD Friday. i will own rollout checklist and canary gates.
Raj: i'll prototype a telemetry dashboard next week for mismatch and provisional rates.
Olivia: i'll add trace/span conventions and decision_id correlation keys to the tracing guide.
admission-bot: reminder: weekly arch sync Fri 10:00am — bring RFC comments.
Emma: created tickets: ADMIT-462 (RFC draft), ADMIT-463 (canary monitoring), ADMIT-464 (dedicated token design). :thumbsup:
